questions.question: The ratio of the number of boys in a school to the total number of boys and girls in that school is 7 ∶ 17. If the number of boys in that school is 1099, then how many girls are there in that school?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of the number of boys in a school to the total number of boys and girls in that school is 7 ∶ 17.

The number of boys in that school is 1099,

**Calculation:**

Let the number of boys be 7x,

So the total number of girls 17x - 7x = 10x

As per the question,

The value of 7x = 1099

The value of 10x is 1099 × 10/7 = 1570

questions.question: Pipe A and pipe B running together can fill a cistern in 6 minutes. If B takes 5 minutes more than A to fill it, then the time in which A and B will fill that cistern separately will be, respectively, __________ .
questions.solution:
Given:

Pipe A and pipe B running together can fill a cistern in 6 minutes.

B takes 5 minutes more than A to fill it. 

 

Concept used:

Efficiency = (Total work / Total time taken)

Efficiency = work done in a single day 

Calculation:

Let Pipe A takes x minutes

So pipe B takes x+5 minutes

As per the question,

1/x + 1/(x+5) = 1/6

2x + 5 = x(x+5) 1/6

12x + 30 = x² + 5x

x2 - 7x - 30 = 0

(x+3)(x-10) = 0

So x = 10 

Time taken by B is 10 + 5 = 15 minutes

**∴ The correct option is 4**

questions.question: If (a³ + b³ + c³ - 3abc) = 405, and (a - b)² + (b - c)² + (c -a)² = 54, find the value of (a + b + c).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Formula: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 1/2 × (a + b + c) × [(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²]

Substitute the given values directly:

405 = 1/2 × (a + b + c) × 54

405 = 27 × (a + b + c) ⇒ a + b + c = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 405

(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)² = 54

**Formula Used:**

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 1/2 × (a + b + c) × [(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²]

**Calculation:**

⇒ 405 = 1/2 × (a + b + c) × 54

⇒ 405 = (a + b + c) × 27

⇒ a + b + c = 405 ÷ 27

⇒ a + b + c = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Form of the Identity

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

Conditional Identity

If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Important Variation

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)[(a + b + c)² − 3(ab + bc + ca)]

questions.question: Pipe A can fill 50% of the tank in 6 hours and pipe B can completely fill the same tank in 18 hours. If both the pipes are opened at the same time, in how much time (in minutes) will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by A to fill 100% = 6 × 2 = 12 hours, B = 18 hours.

Total work (LCM of 12, 18) = 36 units.

Combined Efficiency = (36 ÷ 12) + (36 ÷ 18) = 3 + 2 = 5 units/hr.

Time taken = 36 ÷ 5 hours = (36 ÷ 5) × 60 minutes = 432 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 432 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Pipe A fills 50% of the tank in 6 hours ⇒ It fills 100% of the tank in 12 hours.

Pipe B completely fills the tank in 18 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 12
 36
 3
 
 

 B
 18
 2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total combined efficiency of A and B = 3 + 2 = 5 units/hr

⇒ Time taken to fill the tank together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 36 ÷ 5 hours

⇒ Converting hours to minutes: Time = (36 ÷ 5) × 60

⇒ Time = 36 × 12 = 432 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 432 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Emptying Pipe (Leakage)

If an emptying pipe or leak is present, its efficiency is taken as negative. Net efficiency = (Filling Efficiency) − (Emptying Efficiency).

Fractional Work Method

If pipe A fills a tank in x hours and pipe B fills it in y hours, the part of the tank filled by both in 1 hour is (1/x) + (1/y).

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of time taken by pipe A and pipe B is a : b, then the ratio of their efficiencies will be b : a.
</p

sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B

tanA = 1/√2

B = 90°

A + B + C = 180°

So

A + C = 180° - 90° = 90°

The value of,

sin A cos C + cos A sin C

⇒ sin (A + C)

⇒ sin(90)° 

⇒ 1

**∴ The correct option is** **1**

questions.question:
Which of the following will yield maximum discount on Rs. 7,500?

1. Two successive discounts of 5% and 5%

2. Single discount of 10%

3. Two successive discounts of 8% and 2%

options.text: All will yield the same discount

questions.solution:
**Given:**

1. Two successive discounts of 5% and 5%

2. Single discount of 10%

3. Two successive discounts of 8% and 2%

**Calculation:**

Case 1: Effective discount = 5 + 5 - (5 × 5)/100 = 10 - 0.25 = 9.75%

Case 2: A single discount is always more profitable than two successive discounts of the same value.

A single discount of 10 % is always more profitable.

Case 3: Effective discount = 8 + 2 - (8 × 2)/100 = 10 - 0.16 = 9.84%

**∴ The correct option is** **2**

questions.question: Each inlet pipe can fill an empty cistern in 84 hours while each drain pipe can empty the same cistern from a filled condition in 105 hours. When the cistern is empty, 9 inlet pipes and 10 outlet pipes are simultaneously opened. After how many hours will the cistern be completely filled?
questions.solution:
Given:

Each inlet pipe can fill an empty cistern in 84 hours while each drain pipe can empty the same cistern from a filled condition in 105 hours.

When the cistern is empty, 9 inlet pipes and 10 outlet pipes are simultaneously opened

Concept used:

Efficiency = (Total work / Total time taken)

Efficiency = work done in a single day 

Calculation:

Let total work is 420 units ( LCM of 84 and105 and)

The efficiency of 1 inlet pipe = 420 /84

⇒ 5 units

The efficiency of 1 out let pipe= 420 / 105

⇒ 4 units

The efficiency of 9 inlet pipes = 9 × 5

⇒ 45 units

The efficiency of 10 outlet pipes = 10 × 4

⇒ 40 units

Total efficiency of is (45 - 40) / = 5 units

The time will be 420 / 5 = 84 hrs

**∴ The correct option is 1**

questions.question: In a class of 60 students, there are 35 boys. The average weight of boys is 42 kg and the average weight of the full class is 46.5 kg. Find the average weight of girls in the class.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In a class of 60 students, there are 35 boys.

The average weight of boys is 42 kg and the average weight of the full class is 46.5 kg.

**Calculation:**

The number of girls will be 60 - 35 = 25

The total weight of the boys is

⇒ 42 × 35 = 1470 kg

The total weight of the full class is

⇒ 60 × 46.5 = 2790 kg

The total weight of the girls is 

⇒ 2790 - 1470 = 1320 kg

The average weight of girls in the class is

⇒ 1320 / 25 = 52.80 kg

**∴ The correct option is 3**

questions.solution:

Let Peter gets 100 marks

Then Sam gets 100 - 19 = 81 marks

The marks obtained by Peter is more than the marks obtained by Sam ,
